title: Reliable Adaptive Stopping for Krylov-Shadow Quantum Fisher Information Estimation
summary: Scalable quantum Fisher information (QFI) estimation becomes actionable when the numerical estimate is paired with a trustworthy stopping decision. Krylov-shadow QFI estimation has two resource directions: the Krylov order sets the population resolution, whereas the sample count controls statistical uncertainty at that resolution. We show that treating these directions as one can produce false stops, where a width-based rule reports a narrow interval around a biased low-order estimate.
